affiliations.date_precision: The official Army-entry record carries civilian occupation code 773 on April 13, 1943; NARA's corrected Code No. 30 combines four occupations and names no employer, machine, trade, industry, worksite, or duties.
affiliations.research_notes: The private identifier is exact, while the official Army file spells the surname Burkett. Both forms remain visible. The grouped occupation is not a named employer and the Army-to-OSS sequence is unknown.

affiliations.date_precision: The Pennsylvania Gazette places Burke in New York selling maritime insurance when he met Donovan after Pearl Harbor and says he agreed to join OSS in short order; no company is named.
affiliations.research_notes: This is the best-supported immediate pre-OSS civilian occupation for Edmund Michael Burke. The source does not identify an employer, so no employer or self-employment claim is made.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George N. Burke is confirmed as the Army-entry record spelled George N. Burkett by exact private-identifier agreement.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The visually checked index and official Army file carry the same unique private identifier but different surname endings.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private-identifier agreement plus matching given name and middle initial; the surname discrepancy is preserved as evidence rather than silently corrected.
claims.temporal_assessment: The Army record dates entry to April 13, 1943; it does not establish an OSS transfer date.
claims.match_notes: The private identifier remains withheld. Burke is the immutable indexed spelling; Burkett is an official documented variant.

sources.locator_override: Exact private-identifier record; surname Burkett; identifier withheld

claims.claim_text: At Army entry in April 1943, George N. Burke's civilian occupation was recorded in a group covering shovelmen, cranemen, derrickmen, and hoistmen.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NARA's corrected civilian-occupation list decodes the Army field as a four-role heavy-equipment group and names no employer.
claims.identity_match_assessment: Confirmed by exact private-identifier agreement despite the official surname variant Burkett.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to Army entry on April 13, 1943; pre-OSS but not shown to be the immediate OSS predecessor.
claims.match_notes: The grouped code cannot establish which of four occupations applied, and it supplies no employer, machine, industry, worksite, or duties.

claims.claim_text: Edmund Michael Burke was selling marine insurance in New York when he met William J. Donovan and soon agreed to join OSS.
claims.evidence_excerpt: now married and selling maritime insurance in New York City
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The University of Pennsylvania alumni magazine places maritime-insurance sales immediately before Burke met Donovan and agreed to join OSS in short order.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence from the CIA's explicit Edmund Michael and Mike Burke forms, the indexed Edmund M. Burke name, and the established University of Pennsylvania biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded: the source places Burke in this occupation when he met Donovan and says OSS recruitment followed in short order.
claims.match_notes: The organization is unnamed. The claim is an occupation and immediate affiliation, not a named employer or self-employment finding.

claims.claim_text: The Box 93 Michael Burke row may be another index entry for Edmund Michael ‘Mike’ Burke, but the file-level mapping remains unresolved.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: CIA uses Edmund Michael and Mike for one OSS officer, while the index separately lists Edmund M. Burke and Michael Burke in the same box.

claims.temporal_assessment: The CIA source confirms wartime OSS service for the candidate but does not map the Michael-only index row.
